description:
Redwood Inference is strengthening its Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation by hardening KMS integrations and formalizing key rotation and failure-mode testing procedures across Hosted, Dedicated, and especially Private deployments. The project’s goals are to (1) reduce the blast radius of key compromise and misconfiguration via improved key hierarchy/envelope encryption patterns, (2) make key rotation predictable and low-downtime for operators and customers (including customer-managed KMS in Private), and (3) validate resilience by systematically testing KMS-related failure modes (timeouts, throttling, IAM denies, disabled keys, region/API outages) with clear runbooks and monitoring.

Scope includes: control-plane configuration of KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault where applicable), data-plane encrypt/decrypt paths (DEK/KEK usage, caching and TTLs, retry/backoff/circuit-breaking), rotation workflows (scheduled + emergency), audit logging requirements for key lifecycle events, documentation updates for operators (Confluence + Docs), and a repeatable game-day/test harness for KMS dependency failures. Out of scope: replacing the cryptographic primitives wholesale, or adding entirely new storage backends; changes should be backwards compatible with existing encrypted artifacts and support staged rollouts.

Primary stakeholders: Marcus Lin (Security Eng), Kevin Osei & Hanae Suzuki (Security Eng implementation and integrations), Ethan Park / Benji Okafor / Jordan Lee (Platform control plane + policy), Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (SRE reliability + game days), Kira Thompson & Elliot Price (DevEx docs), and Olga Petrov’s GRC team for evidence/control mapping. Timeline: 6–8 weeks total—week 1 assessment/threat model + design decisions; weeks 2–5 implementation (hardening + rotation plumbing); weeks 4–7 failure-mode tests/game days and operational readiness; weeks 6–8 documentation, training, and gradual rollout (Private first for new installs, then opt-in upgrades, then broader defaults). Deliverables: ADRs and security standards updates, platform changes merged behind flags, runbooks and rotation playbooks, test plan + results, and customer-facing collateral (security FAQ updates, enterprise responses).

files.description: High-level architecture and security overview of Redwood’s KMS integrations: key hierarchy (KEK/DEK), envelope encryption flow, caching strategy, provider support matrix, and explicit threat model (misuse cases, mitigations).
ADR documenting rotation semantics (scheduled vs emergency), backwards compatibility guarantees for existing ciphertext, key version selection rules, and rollback strategy.

SRE runbook for KMS degradation/outage: detection signals, dashboards to check, safe toggles/feature flags, temporary mitigations (cache TTL adjustments, circuit breaker settings), and escalation paths.
Spec for audit events around key creation, rotation, disablement, decrypt failures, and policy denials; includes event schema, retention expectations, and mapping to enterprise controls.

Operator-facing procedure for Private deployments: prerequisites (IAM/KMS policies), step-by-step rotation workflow, validation checklist, common failure cases, and customer responsibilities vs Redwood responsibilities.
Policy/process page defining breakglass access for KMS-related emergencies: approval flow, time-boxing, audit requirements, and post-incident review expectations.
Project umbrella issue: KMS integration hardening + rotation docs. Goals, milestones, sub-issues, owners, and rollout plan across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Implement deterministic key selection + version pinning rules in control plane config (prevent accidental key-version drift during rollouts).
Add circuit breaker + adaptive backoff for KMS calls in data plane; define SLO-aligned thresholds and safe defaults.
Rotation workflow implementation: staged dual-read (old/new key) window, re-encryption job orchestration (where applicable), and validation hooks.
Failure-mode test plan and harness: simulate KMS timeouts/throttling/IAM denies/disabled keys; define expected service behavior and acceptance criteria.
Observability: metrics and tracing for KMS latency/error codes, cache hit rates, circuit breaker state, and per-tenant impact summaries.
Private installer integration: ensure KMS settings are validated at install/upgrade time; add preflight checks for IAM policies and key accessibility.
Docs deliverable tracking: rotation procedure, troubleshooting guide, and security FAQ deltas; coordinate DevEx review and publication.
Security review task: confirm least-privilege IAM templates per provider, define key policy guidance, and review breakglass requirements.
Game day execution issue: schedule and run KMS outage simulation in staging + one canary environment; capture learnings and follow-ups.
PR: Add KMS client circuit breaker and standardized retry/backoff policy; includes config flags, unit tests, and rollout notes.
PR: Introduce key-version pinning in encryption config schema; migration logic and validation errors for unsafe configs.
PR: Emit structured audit events for KMS operations (encrypt/decrypt failures, key-id usage) and integrate with audit logging pipeline.
PR: Implement dual-read window during rotation (attempt decrypt with new key then old) with bounded fallback; includes metrics.
PR: Add chaos/failure injection hooks for KMS calls in staging (timeouts/throttles/AccessDenied) used by the failure-mode test suite.
PR: Add per-tenant KMS health summary endpoint for ops/debug (sanitized), gated behind admin permissions.
PR: Private installer preflight checks for KMS (key reachable, correct region, IAM permissions), plus clearer error messaging.
PR: Update Terraform modules to generate least-privilege IAM/KMS policies and document required key policy statements.
PR: Publish rotation and troubleshooting docs; update enterprise admin/security pages and link to runbooks (with restricted sections).
PR: Add incident-bot snippet templates for KMS incidents (data to capture, links to dashboards/runbooks) to standardize response.
Thread coordinating threat model and design review: key hierarchy, provider differences, and what constitutes ‘rotation complete’ in Private.
Thread on config schema changes (key version pinning, validation) and migration concerns for existing tenants.
Thread tuning circuit breaker thresholds and alerts; discussion on alert fatigue vs catching partial KMS brownouts early.
Thread with Solutions Eng feedback from Private customers: operational constraints, required runbook steps, and IAM policy gotchas.
Thread between DevEx and Security on documentation structure: what is public vs restricted, terminology consistency, and screenshots/log examples.
Thread proposing ADR scope and seeking sign-off on backwards compatibility contract for ciphertext during rotation.
Thread for a staged failure test that unexpectedly caused elevated decrypt failures in a canary; triage notes and rollback decision.
Thread discussing on-call playbook updates: what evidence to collect (error codes, key ids, breaker state) and when to page Security.
Thread reviewing least-privilege policy templates for AWS KMS and how to document customer-managed key policy requirements.
Thread on performance impact: KMS call latency, caching TTL tradeoffs, and how to avoid hot-path regressions.
Thread planning the KMS game day: scenarios, success criteria, comms plan, and required dashboards.
Thread coordinating rollout sequencing, feature flags, and canary tenants for rotation changes; includes release checklist.
Thread relaying an enterprise question about rotation frequency and evidence requirements; links to draft docs and proposed response.
Thread post-game-day debrief: what failed, which alerts fired/didn’t, action items for runbook and code hardening.
Working draft (Q&A format) for enterprise customers: rotation cadence, emergency rotation, key ownership model, audit evidence, and shared responsibility boundaries.
Spreadsheet-style test matrix enumerating KMS failure scenarios, expected behavior, observed results, and follow-up fixes (with links to PRs/issues).
Implementation notes and edge cases discovered while adding installer preflight checks (regional endpoints, IAM propagation delays, key policy pitfalls).
Draft alert review doc: proposed metrics, thresholds, paging policy, and examples of dashboards for KMS latency/error spikes.
Customer ticket: Private deployment rotation attempt led to intermittent decrypt failures; includes logs, environment details, triage comments, and resolution/workaround.
Internal helpdesk ticket: request to grant temporary breakglass access for a staging KMS test; approval trail and audit requirements.

Security/compliance review call transcript with a regulated prospect focusing on customer-managed KMS, rotation cadence, evidence/audit logs, and failure-mode expectations; ends with concrete next steps.
Email thread: prospect security team requests formal KMS rotation procedure and audit event list; includes attachment stubs, versioned doc links, and negotiation on wording/assurances.
CRM company record capturing security requirements (customer-managed KMS, audit logging, rotation evidence), stage notes from security review, blockers, and linked artifacts (Fireflies/Gmail/Drive).
